The air rights issue is very straight forward, private landowners retain rights to exclusive use of the airspace for the reasonable enjoyment of their property up to 500 feet above their lands. However land rights below the ground is a bit more muddled. Do you own the land, do you own the mineral rights. This makes a difference. If you own the mineral rights you have the rights to everything below your land with issues of easements and the like. However, if you find items of historical significances and you want to keep this right, just sell them to someone dont report it. You can lose some rights to your land if say you find a viking burial ground at 20 feet.
